conversation.Statement: Internal Revenue Service, Compliance Division. This is Agent Parker speaking. Who am I speaking with, please?
Um, this is Evelyn Brooks. I just got a message from someone at the IRS and I'm very worried.

Thank you, Ms. Brooks. I'm looking at your profile now. According to our records, there are some irregularities in your recent federal tax filings, specifically regarding your 1099 income and payroll tax compliance. Have you been notified about this before?
No, this is the first I'm hearing about it. I'm retired but I do some crafts and sell a few things, nothing big.

I understand, but even small businesses must comply with IRS regulations. The issue is that certain forms, including 1099s, were not properly filed. This has triggered a non-compliance status on your account.
Oh dear. I didn't realize. What does that mean? Am I in trouble?

Ms. Brooks, failure to resolve this now may result in substantial fines, a federal audit, and possibly even seizure of your bank accounts or Social Security payments. I don't want to see that happen to you.
No, please. I can't lose my Social Security! I rely on that every month.
I want to help you avoid escalation. But this matter is time-sensitive. Can you verify your full address and your date of birth so I can confirm I'm speaking to the correct taxpayer?
Yes, it's 204 Maple Lane, Springfield, and my birthday is March 19, 1952.
Thank you. One more thing: for verification, can you please confirm the last four digits of your Social Security number?

Thank you, Ms. Brooks. Now, per IRS directives, you must settle your outstanding compliance penalty today to prevent further action. You are not to discuss these proceedings with anyone, as it could be considered evidence tampering.
I don't have much money. What exactly do I have to pay?

The immediate penalty is $1,950. If payment is not made today, your case will be forwarded for full criminal investigation and you could lose access to your benefits. Do you have a debit card, credit card, or online banking available?
I have a debit card, but my balance isn't very high. I'm scared.

If you cooperate now, we can set up a payment arrangement. Because of IRS protocols, payments must be made through government-approved vouchers. These can be purchased as prepaid gift cards from a nearby store.
Gift cards? I've never done that before. Are you sure?

That is the required process for urgent compliance settlements. Please do not hang up, and do not speak to anyone while you complete this. Go to your closest Walmart, Target, or CVS. I will tell you exactly what to buy.
I don't drive much. It's a couple miles away. Can I take a taxi?
Yes, please do so immediately. Your case is timed, and failure to comply will result in automated enforcement. Stay on the line with me at all times.
Alright, I'll get ready and call a cab. What do I say if someone asks why I'm buying gift cards?
You must not reveal anything about this IRS case. If a cashier asks, you are buying them for personal reasons. Disclosure could compromise your compliance status.
Okay, I understand. How many cards do I need?
Purchase four cards of $500 each, preferably Apple or Target gift cards. As soon as you buy them, return home and read me the numbers on the back. That will settle your initial penalty.
This is so much money. I hope this works.
You have my assurance, Ms. Brooks. As soon as you provide the codes, I will file your compliance and stop all further actions. Please confirm when you arrive at the store.
